chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Listening to records in Houston: blues and 'Georgia on My Mind'
summary: He first really listened to records on jukeboxes in Houston, hearing blues and Bessie Smith, and loved whistling tunes with his own fill-ins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: But really, for records, really listening to records, was in Houston.
Well, who had a phonograph?
They used to have it --
On the --
On the jukebox. They used to have those, too.
Yeah, well, by this time, this would be about '23, 1923.
Yeah, it was --
Or more, '25.
'24, yeah.
Well, what would you hear?
They were playing a lot of blues and -- what did you say, the Hot Five?
Well, it was too early for the Hot Five.
Well, it could have been, but --
Yeah.
-- they were playing a lot of blues.
Yeah.
Mannie Smith, Bessie Smith.
Oh, Bessie, yeah.
And some band had -- they made a number called Georgia on my Mind.
Yeah.
And that was really one of the best numbers I had heard on a record. It really knocked me out, the way it sounded.
Did you -- you had a feel for melody. Did you whistle, or --
Oh, I always was whistling. Whenever I'd hear -- and it struck me, I would learn it and whistle.
And would you put those little fill-ins or whatnot, or would you just --
I'd put my own fill-ins. I didn't know --
You would put your fill-ins.
Sure, that's right.
Put your own fill-ins. So you could improvise.
Oh, sure, that's right, that's right.
How about that? Isn't that nice? Could you harmonize at all?
